entry_conditions: Enter when the active block is grasped or already in the placement funnel: observations in the assigned slices show fingers nearly closed around 0.018 m and the active block close to the TCP, with red elevated near z=0.28 m at index 185 and blue elevated near z=0.30 m at index 580 in typical demonstrations. The model can also take over during carry-in overlap when the held block is lower but still close to the TCP and moving toward its goal, because it conditions on current block-to-goal residuals rather than on a fixed time index.
exit_conditions: For a red placement exit, the red pose should be near the red goal in world metres with z about 0.036 m, the fingers should be open or opening, and the TCP should have retreated enough not to drag red while control transfers toward blue acquisition. For final blue placement, exit when blue is likewise near the blue goal, both red_at_goal and blue_at_goal are visually represented by the state predicates, and the gripper is open/retreating. These are handoff cues; task success is still defined only by the completion contract.
overlap_role: The policy is trained over the full expanded M1_v2 slice, including carry-in overlaps [185,250) and [580,625) and the red release/retreat transition [330,420). Causal cues available in the observation are object pose relative to its goal, TCP-object offset, object height, qpos finger opening, and short-horizon motion from the two observation frames. These cues let the learned diffusion model continue a predecessor transport phase, descend and release, or produce retreat/transition actions without requiring an external time index.
successor_readiness: The acquire-blue successor is ready after red is settled in the red goal, fingers are open, and the TCP is above/away from red so moving toward the blue block will not disturb it; examples around indices 330-420 show this transition. There is no manipulation successor after final blue placement except task completion monitoring, for which both goal predicates should be true and the TCP should be clear enough not to push either block.
failure_signatures: Do not continue relying on this policy if the inferred active object is not close to the TCP while the fingers are commanded closed, if the gripper opens with the active block high above the tray or outside the target XY tolerance, if the active object z remains high after the intended placement phase, if the inactive block moves noticeably, or if the TCP pushes a placed block along the tray. These are observed-risk signatures, not hard thresholds learned by an external controller.
continuation_guidance: Continue the policy while the active block residual to its goal is decreasing or while the TCP is performing the demonstrated release/retreat after a block has settled. The policy can be invoked partway through a transition because it sees both the current and previous state: a lifted block near the TCP with closed fingers indicates carry/descent, a block at goal with fingers opening indicates release, and an open gripper with the TCP moving away from the placed block indicates transition readiness.
limitations: The handoff assumes successful grasp/contact comparable to the demonstrations and fixed tray/object geometry. It does not certify recovery from dropped objects, wrong block selection, severe collisions, or unobserved clutter. The measured boundary states are evidence of training support and should not be interpreted as a separate scripted acceptance test.
